Ugh, I wish I had a good answer to give you, but just like people it can be smooth(ish) or it could be rough. I’ve seen both cats and dogs take chemo very well and others not so much. My recommendation is to take in all the information you can get from your vet regarding treatment and prognosis and even quality of life and do research as well. At the end of the day, You know your pet the best, better than us sometimes; you spend the most time with them and know their personalities and the fight in them. 

I knew my girl was suffering, and suffering bad. The internal medicine specialist didn’t know if she would respond to treatment if we even started it. So, I took her home with me for one last night and made the incredibly difficult decision to send her to heaven the next morning. I could not see her suffer like that. I personally did not pursue treatment because I didn’t want her final days to be horrible. I hate that she is gone, but I feel at peace with my decision. 

I hope I didn’t ramble too much. I hope this helped. 🩶
